sections.title: Form and flowers
sections.text: Pulsatilla pratensis, a pasqueflower also treated taxonomically as Anemone pratensis, is a small perennial forming a tuft. It reaches about 15 cm in flower and up to 45 cm when fruiting. Its solitary, nodding flowers are about 3–4 cm across.

sections.title: Leaves and fruit
sections.text: The basal leaves are finely divided. After flowering, the fruiting head consists of achenes with long feathery styles.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: Fresh plants in the genus Pulsatilla contain irritating compounds; contact with fresh sap can irritate skin. The available sources do not establish a food use for this species.
